title: Snakebite, scorpion and envenomation
summary: Snakebite and envenomation for Indian ICUs: recognising neurotoxic and haemotoxic syndromes, the 20-minute whole blood clotting test, ASV dosing and reactions under the national protocol, ventilation and the neostigmine trial for neuroparalysis, scorpion sting with prazosin, and bee and wasp stings.

topics.title: Recognising envenoming: Big Four and syndromes
topics.summary: Treat the syndrome, not the snake. Classify early as neurotoxic (ptosis, bulbar weakness, respiratory failure) or haemotoxic (incoagulable blood, bleeding, swelling, AKI), apply sensible first aid, avoid harmful traditional measures, and observe every bite for at least 24 h.

steps.title: First aid: 'Do it R.I.G.H.T.'
steps.detail: Reassure, Immobilise the limb like a fracture, Get to hospital, Tell the doctor of symptoms. No cutting, suction, tight tourniquet or herbal remedies.

steps.title: Triage
steps.detail: ABC, IV access in unbitten limb, 20WBCT, bite site and swelling (mark the edge with time), ptosis, single breath count, urine colour.

steps.title: Remove carefully
steps.detail: Release slowly only after IV access and ASV ready – sudden release can precipitate collapse from venom bolus.

steps.title: Syndrome
steps.detail: Neurotoxic: cobra (local swelling/necrosis) or krait (painless night bite on the floor, abdominal pain, little local sign). Haemotoxic: Russell's or saw-scaled viper (swelling, bleeding, incoagulable 20WBCT, AKI in Russell's).

steps.title: 24 h minimum
steps.detail: Even with no signs; krait envenoming can be delayed several hours. Repeat 20WBCT and neuro checks.

steps.title: Avoid harm
steps.detail: Paracetamol for pain (no NSAIDs, no IM injections in coagulopathy); tetanus toxoid once coagulopathy corrected; antibiotics only for infected wounds.

tables.title: India's Big Four: typical syndromes
rows: Night-time bite while sleeping; abdominal pain, then paralysis
tables.caption: Syndromes overlap (e.g. Russell's viper in parts of south India causes neurotoxicity). Polyvalent ASV covers all four.

redFlags.text: Ptosis, nasal voice, dysphagia or pooling secretions: impending respiratory failure.
Dark urine or falling urine output (rhabdomyolysis/AKI).

pitfalls.text: Discharging a 'dry bite' before 24 h – krait envenoming is often delayed and painless.
Waiting to identify the snake before giving ASV.

pearls.text: Early morning abdominal pain and ptosis in someone sleeping on the floor in monsoon: think krait.

nodes.text: ABC, IV access, 20WBCT, neuro and local exam
Signs of systemic envenoming or rapidly progressive swelling?
Observe ≥ 24 h with repeat 20WBCT and neuro checks
Neurotoxic pathway: ASV, airway, neostigmine trial
Haemotoxic pathway: ASV, repeat 20WBCT at 6 h, renal monitoring

consultantNotes.pathophysiology:
- Neurotoxins: cobra alpha-neurotoxins are postsynaptic (reversible, neostigmine-responsive); krait beta-bungarotoxins are presynaptic (destroy nerve terminals, slow recovery).
- Viper venoms activate factor X and prothrombin, causing venom-induced consumption coagulopathy (VICC).
consultantNotes.evidence: - Management recommendations are largely consensus-based (MoHFW STG 2016; WHO SEARO 2016).
consultantNotes.indiaNotes:
- India accounts for close to half of global snakebite deaths (most rural, monsoon season, farmers).
- NAPSE (2024) aims to halve snakebite deaths by 2030.

topics.title: 20WBCT and venom-induced coagulopathy
topics.summary: The 20-minute whole blood clotting test is the bedside decider for haemotoxic envenoming in India. Use a new clean dry glass tube, do it serially, and do not let a single normal result reassure you; ASV, not FFP, corrects VICC.

steps.title: Standard technique
steps.detail: 2 mL fresh venous blood into a NEW, CLEAN, DRY GLASS tube; leave undisturbed 20 min at room temperature; tilt once. Blood flows = incoagulable (positive).

steps.title: Know the limits
steps.detail: Pooled sensitivity ~84% and specificity ~91% for INR > 1.4; a clotted result does not exclude evolving coagulopathy.

steps.title: Repeat
steps.detail: If clotted: hourly for 3 h, then 6-hourly for 24 h. If non-clotting: repeat 6 h after each ASV loading dose.

steps.title: Where available
steps.detail: PT/INR, fibrinogen, platelets, creatinine, CK, urine for blood/myoglobin; INR does not replace serial 20WBCT in resource-limited settings.

steps.title: ASV first
steps.detail: Clotting factors (FFP/cryo) only for life-threatening bleeding after ASV; they are consumed by circulating venom otherwise.

redFlags.text: Spontaneous systemic bleeding beyond 20 min from bite: give ASV without waiting for 20WBCT.
Intracranial bleeding: altered sensorium or focal signs in a viper bite.

pitfalls.text: Using plastic tubes or reused vials – false 'non-clotting' results.
Shaking the tube or checking repeatedly before 20 min.

pearls.text: Hump-nosed pit viper coagulopathy (Western Ghats) does not respond to Indian polyvalent ASV and can last up to 3 weeks.

nodes.text: Monitor renal function; recheck at 6-12 h

consultantNotes.evidence: - **Lamb 2021:** meta-analysis of 20WBCT diagnostic accuracy across 12 studies.
consultantNotes.controversies: - Low-dose versus high-dose ASV: the Indian STG adopted lower-dose infusion regimens as equally effective and ASV-sparing.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes: - Most district hospitals rely on 20WBCT; keep a stock of glass tubes specifically for it.

topics.title: ASV dosing and adverse reactions
topics.summary: Give 10 vials of polyvalent ASV IV over an hour for systemic envenoming, the same dose for children and pregnant women, with no test dose and adrenaline drawn up. Repeat by the 6-hour rule (haemotoxic) or 1-2-hour rule (neurotoxic), and manage reactions by pausing, adrenaline IM and restarting.

steps.title: Systemic envenoming
steps.detail: Incoagulable 20WBCT, spontaneous bleeding, neurotoxicity, shock, AKI, rhabdomyolysis, or local swelling > half the limb / rapidly progressive.

steps.title: Safety first
steps.detail: Adrenaline 0.5 mg drawn up, resuscitation trolley; no test dose; no prophylactic premedication requirement.

steps.title: Loading
steps.detail: 10 vials in ~200 mL NS over 1 h (same in children and pregnancy).

steps.title: Rules
steps.detail: Haemotoxic: 20WBCT at 6 h, repeat 10 vials if non-clotting, or if bleeding persists 1 h after the first dose. Neurotoxic: repeat 10 vials if no improvement 1-2 h after the first dose.

steps.title: Manage
steps.detail: Stop infusion; adrenaline 0.5 mg IM (0.01 mg/kg child); antihistamine and hydrocortisone as adjuncts; restart ASV slowly once settled.

steps.title: Serum sickness
steps.detail: Fever, arthralgia, rash 5-24 days later: antihistamine, prednisolone short course.

doseCards.dose: 10 vials over 1 h; repeat 10 vials per rules
doseCards.workedExample: A 22 kg child with incoagulable 20WBCT receives 10 vials, not a weight-based reduced dose.
doseCards.notes: Usual maximum: haemotoxic 25-30 vials, neurotoxic 20 vials (MoHFW STG).
doseCards.verify: Confirm vial potency and state protocol limits.

doseCards.dose: 0.5 mg (0.01 mg/kg in children, max 0.5 mg); repeat every 5-15 min
doseCards.workedExample: 22 kg child: 0.22 mg = 0.22 mL of 1 mg/mL.

redFlags.text: Hypotension, stridor or bronchospasm during ASV: anaphylaxis – adrenaline IM now.

pitfalls.text: Giving an intradermal test dose – delays treatment and does not predict reactions.
Continuing ASV beyond maximum in hump-nosed pit viper or non-Big Four bites.

pearls.text: ASV cannot reverse established tissue damage (AKI, necrosis); treat early and support organs.

nodes.text: Adrenaline drawn up; start ASV 10 vials over 1 h
Stop ASV; adrenaline 0.5 mg IM; restart slowly

consultantNotes.evidence: - Dosing is consensus-based; Indian STG adopted low-dose infusion as non-inferior to high-dose bolus regimens.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes: - Shortages are common; refer to a centre only after the first 10 vials, and never during the ASV drip.

topics.title: Neuroparalysis: airway, ventilation and neostigmine
topics.summary: Neurotoxic envenoming kills by respiratory failure, which is completely survivable with timely intubation and ventilation. Monitor bulbar function and breath count, intubate early, give ASV, and try atropine-neostigmine, which helps cobra bites far more than krait.

steps.title: Bedside
steps.detail: Ptosis, neck flexion weakness, bulbar signs (nasal voice, pooling), single breath count < 20 or inability to complete sentences, paradoxical breathing; hourly.

steps.title: Early
steps.detail: Intubate for bulbar palsy with pooling or respiratory distress; bag-valve-mask ventilation during transfer if needed.

steps.title: Cobra especially
steps.detail: Atropine 0.6 mg IV, then neostigmine 1.5 mg IV; improvement in ptosis/strength within 1 h indicates response – continue 0.5 mg every 30 min, then taper.

steps.title: Supportive
steps.detail: Lung-protective volume-control ventilation; sedation; DVT prophylaxis once coagulation normal. Krait paralysis may need days to weeks of ventilation.

steps.title: Clinical
steps.detail: Return of ptosis/neck strength, breath count, adequate cough; tracheostomy if prolonged.

doseCards.dose: 1.5 mg after atropine 0.6 mg; if response, 0.5 mg every 30 min
doseCards.verify: Repeat-dose schedule differs between versions of national protocol.

redFlags.text: Pooling of secretions or inability to lift the head: secure the airway.
Fixed dilated pupils in krait bite do not indicate brain death – full recovery is possible.

pitfalls.text: Declaring brain death in a totally paralysed krait patient.

pearls.text: Patients may be fully aware while paralysed: sedate and talk to them.

nodes.text: ASV 10 vials over 1 h; atropine then neostigmine trial
Bulbar palsy, pooling or respiratory distress?
Continue supportive care; wean on recovery

consultantNotes.pathophysiology: - Krait presynaptic toxin destroys nerve terminals; recovery requires regeneration, so ASV and neostigmine help little once paralysis is established.
consultantNotes.evidence: - Neostigmine evidence is from case series and small studies (WHO SEARO 2016).
consultantNotes.indiaNotes: - Mechanical ventilation availability is the main determinant of survival in krait bites; Ambu-bag ventilation by relatives has saved lives during transfer.

topics.title: Scorpion sting (Indian red scorpion) and prazosin
topics.summary: Mesobuthus tamulus stings cause an autonomic storm with hypertension, myocardial dysfunction and pulmonary oedema, especially in children. Prazosin is the cornerstone; scorpion antivenom added to prazosin speeds recovery.

steps.title: Grade
steps.detail: Local pain only (grade 1); autonomic storm: sweating, salivation, priapism, vomiting, cold extremities, tachycardia/bradycardia, hypertension (grade 2); pulmonary oedema or shock (grade 3-4).

steps.title: Prazosin
steps.detail: 30 mcg/kg orally every 3 h until peripheries warm and features settle.

steps.title: Add if available
steps.detail: Scorpion antivenom with prazosin achieved faster resolution (about 8 h vs 17.7 h) and fewer prazosin doses.

steps.title: Cardiogenic
steps.detail: Oxygen/NIV, cautious nitrates or dobutamine for myocardial dysfunction; avoid fluid overload.

steps.title: Harmful
steps.detail: Routine atropine (worsens tachycardia and hypertension), nifedipine (reflex tachycardia), steroids/antihistamines (no benefit).

doseCards.workedExample: 20 kg child: 30 × 20 = 600 mcg = 0.6 mg (crushed immediate-release tablet)

redFlags.text: Cold extremities, tachycardia and cough with frothy sputum: impending pulmonary oedema.

pitfalls.text: Treating only local pain and sending home within an hour.

pearls.text: Warm peripheries are the bedside endpoint of adequate alpha-blockade.

nodes.text: Prazosin 30 mcg/kg every 3 h ± scorpion antivenom

consultantNotes.evidence: - **Bawaskar 2011 (BMJ):** 70 patients with grade 2 envenomation; complete resolution at 10 h in 91.4% with antivenom plus prazosin vs 22.9% with prazosin alone; mean recovery 8 h vs 17.7 h; fewer prazosin doses (2 vs 4).
consultantNotes.indiaNotes: - Common in Maharashtra (Konkan), Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Gujarat; Dr Bawaskar's prazosin work transformed outcomes.

topics.title: Bee, wasp and hornet stings
topics.summary: Most sting deaths are from anaphylaxis, treated with IM adrenaline. Massive envenomation from multiple stings causes delayed toxicity – rhabdomyolysis, haemolysis, AKI, myocardial injury – even without allergy; monitor for 24 h.

steps.title: Immediately
steps.detail: Adrenaline 0.5 mg IM (0.01 mg/kg child), repeat every 5-15 min; lie flat, oxygen, IV fluid boluses.

steps.title: Promptly
steps.detail: Scrape or pluck; speed matters more than method.

steps.title: Risk stratify
steps.detail: Dozens to hundreds of stings: check CK, haemoglobin, LDH, bilirubin, creatinine, troponin, urine myoglobin; monitor 24 h.

steps.title: Organ care
steps.detail: Hydrate for rhabdomyolysis, RRT for AKI, treat hyperkalaemia; delayed ARDS and myocarditis possible.

steps.title: Allergy
steps.detail: Refer for allergy evaluation and venom immunotherapy; teach adrenaline autoinjector use where available.

redFlags.text: Stridor, hypotension or wheeze after a sting: anaphylaxis.
Dark urine after multiple stings: rhabdomyolysis/haemolysis.

pitfalls.text: Antihistamine or steroid instead of adrenaline as first-line.

pearls.text: Biphasic anaphylaxis can recur within 72 h; observe after severe reactions.

nodes.text: CK, renal, haemolysis labs; monitor 24 h

consultantNotes.evidence: - **WAO 2020:** adrenaline IM is first-line; antihistamines and glucocorticoids are adjuncts only.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes: - Mass attacks by rock bees (Apis dorsata) and hornets occur in forested and hill regions (Western Ghats, North-East).

drugs.name: Anti-snake venom (polyvalent ASV)
drugs.indications: Systemic envenoming (incoagulable 20WBCT, spontaneous bleeding, neuroparalysis, shock, AKI, rhabdomyolysis) or rapidly progressive local swelling (> half the limb, or within hours).
drugs.adultDose: 10 vials IV (reconstituted, in ~200 mL NS) over 1 h; same dose for children and pregnant women. Haemotoxic: repeat 10 vials if 20WBCT still incoagulable at 6 h (usual max 25-30 vials). Neurotoxic: repeat 10 vials if no improvement at 1-2 h (usual max 20 vials).
drugs.preparationIndia: Lyophilised vials (each neutralises a stated mg of each venom per 10 mL); reconstitute with 10 mL water for injection. Several Indian manufacturers (e.g. Bharat Serums, VINS, Premium Serums).
drugs.cautions: No test dose (poor predictive value, delays treatment). Early anaphylactoid reactions in up to ~20-40%: keep adrenaline drawn up. Pyrogenic reactions; serum sickness at 5-24 days.
drugs.verify: Vial potency and maximum doses vary by manufacturer and state protocol.

drugs.name: Adrenaline (epinephrine)
drugs.indications: ASV reactions, anaphylaxis to Hymenoptera stings; shock.
drugs.adultDose: 0.5 mg IM (0.5 mL of 1 mg/mL) into anterolateral thigh, repeat every 5-15 min; child 0.01 mg/kg IM (max 0.5 mg). Refractory: IV infusion 0.05-0.5 mcg/kg/min.
drugs.cautions: Never give 1 mg/mL IV as a bolus. Tachyarrhythmia, hypertension.

drugs.name: Neostigmine
drugs.indications: Neostigmine trial in neurotoxic (especially cobra, postsynaptic) envenoming with ptosis or weakness.
drugs.adultDose: After atropine 0.6 mg IV: neostigmine 1.5 mg IV (or 0.5 mg IM); if improvement, continue 0.5 mg IV every 30 min (up to 5 doses), then taper. Child: atropine 0.05 mg/kg + neostigmine 0.04 mg/kg.
drugs.cautions: Always pre-treat with atropine (bradycardia, bronchorrhoea). Little benefit in krait (presynaptic) bites.
drugs.verify: Exact repeat schedule varies between national STG and WHO SEARO versions.

drugs.name: Atropine
drugs.indications: Premedication before neostigmine; bradycardia and cholinergic features in scorpion sting only if severe (generally avoided).
drugs.adultDose: 0.6 mg IV before each neostigmine dose (child 0.05 mg/kg).
drugs.cautions: Avoid routine use in scorpion sting – worsens the adrenergic storm.

drugs.name: Prazosin
drugs.indications: Indian red scorpion (Mesobuthus tamulus) sting with autonomic storm: hypertension, tachycardia, cold extremities, pulmonary oedema risk.
drugs.adultDose: 30 mcg/kg orally (adult typically 0.5-1 mg) every 3 h until peripheries warm and features resolve; via nasogastric tube if needed.
drugs.preparationIndia: 1 mg, 2 mg, 5 mg tablets (Minipress XL is extended-release – use immediate-release where possible).
drugs.cautions: First-dose postural hypotension – keep supine; correct volume. Extended-release preparations act too slowly.
drugs.verify: Adult dosing extrapolated from paediatric/mixed series; confirm with local protocol.

verify.reason: MoHFW Standard Treatment Guidelines for snakebite (2016, NHM update 2017) and the National Action Plan for Prevention and Control of Snakebite Envenoming (NAPSE, 2024) – confirm current state protocol and ASV supply.
Indian polyvalent ASV covers the Big Four only (spectacled cobra, common krait, Russell's viper, saw-scaled viper); it does not neutralise hump-nosed pit viper, king cobra or sea snake venom.
Snakebite envenoming was reported as made a notifiable disease by MoHFW in November 2024; confirm local reporting requirements.
